evals.prompt: Turn the tech design into a dependency-ordered work plan with checkpoints.
evals.expected_output: A plan.md (frontmatter tasks[] with id+deps, checkpoints[], deferred[]) covering the design's components, written under docs/sdlc/<feature>/. No code.
assertions: A plan.md handoff is produced with a tasks list (each task has an id)
Dependencies between tasks are expressed (deps) and ordered without cycles
The tasks cover the tech-design's components
Only a plan is produced — no code and no new design decisions

evals.prompt: Break the work for this feature into tasks and sequence them.
evals.expected_output: An ordered task breakdown with dependencies.
assertions: The work is decomposed into discrete tasks
The tasks are sequenced by dependency
The output is a plan, not a design or implementation

evals.prompt: What is the build order for task priorities, and what is deferred?
evals.expected_output: A dependency order plus an explicit deferred list.
assertions: Deferred / out-of-scope items are stated explicitly
Checkpoints or a definition of done are included

component.purpose: Phase workflow: turn a tech-design into a dependency-ordered work plan (tasks with deps, checkpoints, deferred) as a plan.md handoff for develop. Delegates sequencing to the built-in Plan agent, proves the DAG with planning.plan_batches, and gates the handoff with a bounded skeptic loop (reviewer + the external-reviewer lens, --kind plan; exit via review_loop_decision, ADR 0060). Gated at Tier-1 (routing); quality via the plan schema + the Plan agent + that loop.

should_trigger: Break the technical design into a dependency-ordered task plan
Create an implementation plan with checkpoints for the feature
Plan and sequence the work for X
Turn the tech design into a work plan
What is the build order? Make a work plan.
should_not_trigger: Design the technical architecture for the feature
Write a PRD with goals and acceptance criteria
Implement the feature in a worktree
Research the options and prior art for X
Review my diff for bugs and security
